This is such a good point. Im in high school myself and I am so sick of male pears justifying a discontent towards loud or opinionated feminists by saying they just don’t like *radical* feminism/feminists, when they clearly do not even understand what that term means.

The model minority myth is kind of a bigger thing that many stereotypes play into. Its pretty damaging for a lot of reasons, no one really has the time to get upset every time it happens but I don’t think its stooping low.  It kinda sucks its something you would even have to consider spending time on, because the expectations shouldn’t exist. I doubt you really care enough to bother but here is a link with some possible effects from the model minority myth: https://cmhc.utexas.edu/modelminority.html

You may also find it worth while to further explore the model minority myth because its a super broad and important topic...
I totally understand. I still live in a predominantly white community, but I struggle sometimes with some stereotypes.

YTA,

OP the situation you had with your step father is very different from the one you explain here. You haven’t even *met* your husbands daughter... Your husband of *3* years. Honestly I cannot believe that you have managed to go out of your way for so long to avoid meeting her. It seems a bit irrational tbh. 

I think you should suck up the fact you don’t want to be a step mother and just meet your husband’s daughter. You married this man after all. Shes his daughter and that will not change. She will always be there. 10 years from now will you still be avoiding any contact with her? Because she will always be in your husbands life. When you married him you also committed to everything else he came with. Daughter included. Even if it was established you didnt want to be a mom before, you married a man with a child. Thats that.


EDIT: I just want to add that not everyone is happy with this arrangement. Your husbands ex is unhappy, and the child is wanting to meet you. In the future when the child is more mature she may come to feel the way her mother does in regards to your presence in her life as her dad’s partner.

I understand that, what I mean really is just meet her, and that is, if she wants it (I feel her questions about you will eventually lead to that). You don’t have to be a parent for her. Being a parent is more than just being married to her father and seeing her. You don’t need to get her ready for school, help with homework, or support her really. 

Plus I don’t see this child as an adult wanting to hang out with a woman who has been indirectly a part of her life for 13 years, but hasn’t met her solely because she didn’t want to be a mother. Its kind of selfish on your part really.

You come off a little bit like you have already decided that this situation works for you... why did you even make the post in the first place? It seems a little bit like you came for validation. 


Also I think you mis the mark on this point that she might not want to meet you in the future and how it would be awkward... she’s technically family now. It could put a wrench in her future relationship with her father when milestones of her life come along.
